A spline says it goes on into another on: A spline says it goes on into another one that no longer exists. "Fix" forgets that link.
A bus stop belongs to the lane it stands: A bus stop belongs to the lane it stands beside (within about 25 m). This one has none near, so buses cannot stop at it. Move it next to the road, or "Fix" puts it at the kerb of the nearest lane (within 80 m).
A start point is where the bus appears. This one is away from any lane: fine in a depot yard, otherwise the bus starts off the road.
A start point refers to an object that w: A start point refers to an object that was deleted. "Fix" removes the start point.
There is nowhere for the bus to appear. Place a start point (Game logic > Start points) on a road, or "Fix" puts one on a lane some 40 m before a bus stop.
Two things on the map share one IDCode:: Two things on the map share one IDCode: links, timetables and start points may pick the wrong one.
The counter for new IDCodes is below cod: The counter for new IDCodes is below codes already used, so new objects would get codes twice. "Fix" raises it.
An object standing on the ground lies ou: An object standing on the ground lies outside its own tile. The game does not show it. Move it a little or put it again.
global.cfg lists tiles whose file is not: global.cfg lists tiles whose file is not there. The game leaves them out; they stay listed, as start points and timetables count tiles by their place in the list.
A tile has no height file: its ground is: A tile has no height file: its ground is flat. Saving writes one.

A tour names no depot or group of the AI: A tour names no depot or group of the AI lists (or one that is not there): the game has no vehicle to send on it. Choose a depot for it in the Lines window, or "Fix" gives it the map's depot (one of OMSI 2's MAN buses added where the map has none).
The unscheduled traffic names a group th: The unscheduled traffic names a group that the AI lists do not have: those cars never appear. Add the group in Map > Traffic and AI, or "Fix" copies it from OMSI 2's own maps where they have it.

A chrono scenario takes away, retypes or: A chrono scenario takes away, retypes or relabels something that is no longer on the map (it was deleted or its IDCode changed): that change does nothing. Open Map > Chrono scenarios, the scenario's properties, and take the change out.
A tile holds far more objects than the s: A tile holds far more objects than the stock maps' tiles (up to some 600): the game may stutter when it loads it or looks across it. Thin out a wood planted too densely (Plant brush, Clear) or plant it with more space between the trees.
Street lamps stand on a tile the game do: Street lamps stand on a tile the game does not light from its lamps ([variable_terrainlightmap] is off): at night the ground under them stays dark (unless the tile's light map file was made by OMSI 2's editor). "Fix" turns it on, as on nearly every tile of the stock maps.
